caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

The figure presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, with perplexity on the vertical axis and sparsity rate on the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, representing perplexity, is labeled and has a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, with major ticks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, and minor ticks at intervals of $10^1$. The horizontal axis, representing sparsity rate, is labeled and ranges from $10\%$ to $80\%$ in increments of $10\%$. 

There are two data series: Per-Output and Per-Layer, represented by blue and orange bars, respectively. Each series consists of 9 bars, corresponding to the 9 sparsity rates. The bars for both series are relatively short for sparsity rates up to $50\%$, with Per-Output and Per-Layer perplexity values both below $10^1$. For sparsity rates above $50\%$, the bars for both series increase in height, with the Per-Output bars being noticeably taller than the Per-Layer bars at $60\%$, $70\%$, and $80\%$ sparsity rates. At $60\%$ sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately $15$ while the Per-Layer bar remains near $10^1$. At $70\%$ sparsity, the Per-Output bar climbs to roughly $50$ while the Per-Layer bar reaches approximately $25$. At $80\%$ sparsity, both bars approach $10^3$, with the Per-Output bar exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than the Per-Layer bar.

The bars are not sorted in any specific order other than corresponding to the sparsity rates on the horizontal axis. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or contouring.
